parsed.explanation: The combined national/division regime creates severe traveler-facing exposure. Visa and document screening can trigger refusals or fraud findings; passports/identity rules are contested but restrictive; federal and school facility rules force birth-sex use, including visitors; and custody is documented as harsh: immigration forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; corrections converts trans status into coercive care denial. Local service remedy was removed. Legal challenges, injunctions and marriage/equality formalities do not offset active traveler restrictions. Absence of street-violence counts is not safety. The dossier lacks near-certain execution, but state-directed severity, universal exclusion and failed recourse place it high risk, below 0.35 and above 0.15.

entry_documents.exposure: Visa/border screening treats sex-marker/body/document mismatch as refusal and possible material fraud leading lifetime ineligibility; passport-X rules, reported confiscation/blocking, stranded travelers, foreign advisories and detention reports.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration and courts challenge some passport orders; no documented protection overrides screening.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch can trigger investigation/immigration detention, feeding custody exposure; legal-aid FAQ does not neutralize.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, guards hostility, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopts conversion-therapy-like rules: hair cut, hormones removed, denial of care, stopped prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Challenges/blocking of some orders; pretrial release in one arrest; no documented remedy for immigration/corrections abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If detained for visa fraud, school/facility violation or police stop, traveler enters same hostile placement system.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars gender-congruent use of government-funded single-sex spaces; division school rule binds all people on grounds to birth-certificate facilities; many states have bans and some criminal trespass for refusal; one capitol arrest/handcuffed/men’s ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some jurisdictions/private settings lack mapped bans; exemptions for emergencies/children; no offset to federal or school rules.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility exclusion plus school-rule enforcement creates continuous discovery/humiliation risk in schools, campuses, public buildings.

care_services.exposure: Custody rules deny hormone medication; no documented emergency/visitor care shield. HRT customs, ward placement, outpatient care and minor healthcare access are unresolved.
care_services.protection: No traveler-specific care protection documented; some court injunctions remain general and uncertain.
care_services.interaction: Illness/injury or medication loss can force contact with facilities, border and custody systems, compounding outing exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National policies redefine sex binary, purge trans language, restrict funding, counterterrorism names radically pro-transgender groups; high public support for birth-sex rules; officials frame trans presence as deception/risk.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Marriage recognition, employment ruling, hate-crime statute and litigation exist but are not offsetting protections.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises likelihood of screening, detention and hostile service encounters; removal of local remedy worsens severity.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division school rule requires students, guardians and visitors to use birth-certificate single-sex facilities; students may use single-person only with guardian consent; rules chill adults supporting minors social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Limited exemptions/accompanying children and guardian-consent single-person stalls are narrow; no traveler-family shield.
minors_guardians.interaction: Trans adults at school events, camps or family travel face same facility/outing exposure; minor mismatch interacts with custody.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific street-violence/homicide rate or police profiling pattern documented; monitoring counts are undercounts; police response to trans victims unknown.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and some court protections exist, but division withdrew gender-identity remedy; enforcement uncertain.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Even if violence is not quantified, any police stop can lead to facility/custody exposure; unknown not safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division removed civil-rights remedy for service/housing/job; many states lack bias statutes; school-rule enforcement against adults unclear; border fraud fact-specific.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation, injunctions, legal-aid FAQs and national hate-crime/marriage formalities remain partial.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved legal battles and absent local remedy leave traveler-facing rules operating; unknown practice cannot be read as safe.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A has mandatory presentation offence, regular sweeps, months imprisonment and custody assault. This dossier lacks blanket identity arrest and execution, but has severe custody/visa exposure, so it sits above 0.15.

0.25-C combines parent presentation offence, passport extortion, birth-sex custody abuse and mixed relief. This has no blanket presentation arrest, but visa fraud, immigration sexual abuse and no local remedy make it broadly comparable, slightly lower than 0.25-C.

0.35-A has universal birth-sex public-building rule with rejected complaints but no documented visa fraud, immigration sexual abuse or removal of all local service remedies; this combined regime is materially lower despite polite street/service notes.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is not simply conservative society; federal/division policies weaponize documents, facilities, custody and local remedies. A visitor whose presentation or papers mismatch can face visa denial/fraud, exclusion from gender-congruent facilities at federal/school settings, and if detained severe sexual abuse or forced labour. Withdrawal of local protections means ordinary refusals and harassment have no state/province remedy. Litigation and injunctions create uncertainty but do not erase in-force rules. Because severity is high and exposure universal/institutional, score below 0.35; absence of street-violence counts and execution risk keeps above 0.15.
